answer: A bond of 58% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in spiral, and thread reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 118 aliases, and each one needs its own funded yarrow account. That bill is paid per identity, so 269 aliases cost 44 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
